sentences.en: Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's pretty good.

sentences.en: Coral, this is a policy discussion, ultimately, about Joe Biden's climate plan.
sentences.zh: 科拉，这归根结底是一场关于乔·拜登气候计划的政策讨论。

sentences.en: But just to start, I wonder if you can conjure the Biden climate agenda as a kind of vision that people will experience themselves.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我想知道你是否能将拜登的气候议程描绘成一种人们能够亲身体验的愿景。

sentences.en: Let's say it's 2035 and everything that this new administration wants to get done on climate has actually gotten done.
sentences.zh: 假设现在是2035年，这届新政府在气候方面想要完成的一切都已经真正实现了。

sentences.en: What does life look like?
sentences.zh: 生活会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Given that that's a big if, if everything really gets done, then here's what life would look like.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这是一个很大的假设，如果一切真的实现了，那么生活会是这样的。

sentences.en: You would wake up in your home as a regular American, turn on your lights, turn on your coffee maker, you'd make your breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 作为一个普通的美国人，你会在家中醒来，打开灯，开启咖啡机，准备早餐。

sentences.en: And all of your electricity would now be coming from wind, solar, nuclear, none of it would be coming, none of it, from coal, natural gas, fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 你所有的电力现在都来自风能、太阳能和核能，没有任何电力来自煤炭、天然气或化石燃料。

sentences.en: And if you were to follow those electric wires to the power plant where they came from,
sentences.zh: 如果你顺着那些电线找到它们来源的发电厂，

sentences.en: it would look nothing like the electric power plant that you grew up with in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 它看起来将与你在20世纪成长过程中所见过的发电厂完全不同。

sentences.en: It would look like a gigantic battery that was sucking in wind and solar power that was generated from, you know,
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像一个巨大的电池，吸收着来自，你知道的，

sentences.en: mountaintops or sunny deserts hundreds or thousands of miles away coming into that big battery storing there and coming into your house.
sentences.zh: 数百甚至数千英里外的山顶或阳光充足的沙漠所产生的风能和太阳能，汇入那个大电池中储存，然后再输送到你的家中。

sentences.en: So basically the way the lights turn on would be completely different.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，灯光亮起的方式将完全不同。

sentences.en: And then you would get into your car, which, if the Biden vision is implemented, would almost assuredly not be powered by a combustion engine.
sentences.zh: 然后你会坐进你的车里，如果拜登的愿景得以实现，它几乎肯定不会再由内燃机驱动。

sentences.en: It would be an electric car, but it wouldn't be a fancy Tesla or Prius.
sentences.zh: 它会是一辆电动汽车，但不会是那种花哨的特斯拉或普锐斯。

sentences.en: Ideally, it would be something, you know, big enough that you can put your family in and go for weekend camping trips and haul stuff around and take your kid to college.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，它会是那种足够大、能载着家人去周末露营、搬运东西以及送孩子上大学的车。

sentences.en: It would be a big, regular American car, probably made by GM or Ford, and you would drive to work.
sentences.zh: 它会是一辆大型的、普通的美国车，很可能是通用或福特制造的，你会开着它去上班。

sentences.en: Perhaps you'd realize, oh, no, I'm not charged up.
sentences.zh: 也许你会意识到，哦，糟糕，我没电了。

sentences.en: And you'd pull over, you'd plug in, you would charge it in the same amount of time that it once took you to pump the gas.
sentences.zh: 你会靠边停车，插上电源，充电所需的时间和你曾经加油的时间一样长。

sentences.en: And maybe there would be these new charging stations where you would go in and you would buy your Doritos and your newspaper if, you know,
sentences.zh: 也许会有一些新的充电站，你进去买点多力多滋和报纸，如果，你知道的话，

sentences.en: I hope to God newspapers will still be around.
sentences.zh: 我向上帝祈祷报纸还能存在。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Maybe not.
sentences.zh: 也许不会了。

sentences.en: Well, Coral, that is a hell of a different warning that you have described than what I think most of us have experienced in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，科拉，你所描述的景象与我们大多数人过去所经历的简直是天壤之别。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And here is the other thing that would be profoundly different.
sentences.zh: 还有另一件事会发生深刻的变化。

sentences.en: And this is really important because this is the reason why they're doing all that.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要，因为这就是他们做这一切的原因。

sentences.en: It's not to promote electric cars.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是为了推广电动汽车。

sentences.en: It's not to promote wind and solar.
sentences.zh: 也不是为了推广风能和太阳能。

sentences.en: The other thing that would be different is that maybe your basement wouldn't be flooding because of stronger storms and rising sea levels.
sentences.zh: 另一件会改变的事情是，也许你的地下室不会因为更猛烈的风暴和海平面上升而淹水了。

sentences.en: If you live in the West, maybe you're not looking out the window at thick black skies as another record wildfire sweeps through the mountains near your neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在西部，也许你不用再看着窗外厚重漆黑的天空，看着另一场破纪录的野火席卷你家附近的群山。

sentences.en: Maybe you're not paying two and three and four times as much for your food because we're having extreme droughts that are hurting our agriculture sector and making it harder to get crops.
sentences.zh: 也许你不用再为食物支付两倍、三倍甚至四倍的价格，因为我们正在经历极端干旱，这损害了我们的农业部门，使农作物更难获得。

sentences.en: Those are the impacts of climate change,
sentences.zh: 这些都是气候变化的影响，

sentences.en: of more fossil fuels in the atmosphere that science is saying is also going to be coming down the pike in 10 or 15 years if these policies aren't put in place.
sentences.zh: 是大气中更多化石燃料带来的后果，科学界表示，如果这些政策不落实，未来10到15年内这些情况也会接踵而至。

sentences.en: So those are changes that if the fossil fuel emissions really are stopped, you won't be experiencing those.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果化石燃料排放真的被停止，你将不会再经历这些变化。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And of course, this is a very different vision than the one put forth by the previous president.
sentences.zh: 当然，这与前任总统提出的愿景截然不同。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: President Trump openly mocked the science of human-caused climate change, withdrew the United States from the International Paris Agreement,
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统公开嘲笑人为气候变化的科学，让美国退出了国际《巴黎协定》，

sentences.en: which is the global accord in which pretty much every country in the world said that they would act to reduce their carbon emissions,
sentences.zh: 这是一项全球协议，世界上几乎每个国家都承诺采取行动减少碳排放，

sentences.en: and rolled back over 100 federal environmental protections during his four years in office.
sentences.zh: 并且在他执政的四年里，撤销了100多项联邦环境保护措施。

sentences.en: Biden is essentially doing a sharp U-turn from that.
sentences.zh: 拜登本质上是在进行一个急转弯。

sentences.en: And the goals that he is setting are incredibly aggressive.
sentences.zh: 他设定的目标极其激进。

sentences.en: And I should say, it's not just a U-turn from Trump.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，这不仅仅是对特朗普政策的逆转。

sentences.en: He's going way further than Obama tried to go.
sentences.zh: 他比奥巴马尝试做的要走得远得多。

sentences.en: So Biden's objectives are to eliminate all CO2 from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，拜登的目标是到2050年消除美国经济中所有的二氧化碳排放。

sentences.en: economy by 2050.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其激进的目标。

sentences.en: That is an incredibly aggressive goal.
sentences.zh: 他设定的另一个目标是到2035年，即15年后，实现电力部门和发电厂的零排放。

sentences.en: And then the other goal that he has set is zero emissions from the electricity sector, from power plants, by 2035, 15 years from now.
sentences.zh: 这意味着15年后，我们将不再在美国看到以化石燃料为动力的发电厂。

sentences.en: That is saying 15 years from now, we will no longer see fossil fuel-fired power plants in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 同样，这是一个极其雄心勃勃的目标。

sentences.en: Again, that is an incredibly ambitious goal.
sentences.zh: 这也完全符合科学家所说的为了避免地球变暖带来最灾难性后果所必须采取的行动。

sentences.en: It is also exactly in line with what scientists say is required to avoid the most devastating effects of a warming planet.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，这并不是为了避免全球变暖的影响。

sentences.en: And I should say, not to avoid the impacts of global warming.
sentences.zh: 那些影响显然已经开始，它们将持续存在，并且会变得更糟。

sentences.en: Those have very clearly already started, and they're here to stay, and they're going to get worse.
sentences.zh: 这是在谈论如何让地球保持安全，让人类能够继续生存。

sentences.en: This is talking about keeping the planet safe for people to live in at all.
sentences.zh: 那么拜登总统任命了谁来负责将这一极其激进的愿景变为现实呢？

sentences.en: And who has President Biden put in charge of trying to turn this very aggressive vision into reality?
sentences.zh: 他安排了哪些人？

sentences.en: Who has he put in place?
sentences.zh: 所以拜登总统在这里做了一些新的尝试。

sentences.en: So President Biden has done something new here.
sentences.zh: 他设立了一种双管齐下的白宫气候沙皇职位。

sentences.en: He has created kind of a double-pronged White House climate czar position.
sentences.zh: 他挑选了两位气候政策界的超级明星来担任此职。

sentences.en: He has tapped two sort of superstars of the climate policy world to do it.
sentences.zh: 其中一个职位是约翰·克里，他当然曾是奥巴马政府的国务卿。

sentences.en: In one position, you have John Kerry, who, of course, was the Secretary of State in the Obama administration.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是2015年《巴黎气候变化协定》的核心谈判代表。

sentences.en: He was basically the central negotiator of the 2015 Paris Climate Change Agreement.
sentences.zh: 这就是他将为拜登总统扮演的角色。

sentences.en: That is the role that he will play for President Biden.
sentences.zh: 他将成为某种国际气候特使，他的工作是奔走于世界各地，说，看，美国正在采取行动，我们正在削减排放，我们正在努力工作，你们也必须这样做。

sentences.en: He will be kind of an international climate envoy whose job is to go around the world, say, look, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是我们必须共同努力的方式。

sentences.en: is acting, we're cutting our emissions, we're working hard, you guys have to do it too.
sentences.zh: 他还将——这一点非常重要——在白宫国家安全委员会拥有一席之地。

sentences.en: Here's how we have to do this together.
sentences.zh: 这是新的。

sentences.en: He will also, and this is very important, he will have a seat at the White House National Security Council.
sentences.zh: 以前从未发生过。

sentences.en: That's new.
sentences.zh: 这意味着气候变化现在将成为白宫每一项重大国家安全和外交政策决策中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: That's never happened.
sentences.zh: 它将在决策桌上占有一席之地，而约翰·克里，作为一名资深人士，在许多方面比桌上的其他人拥有更深厚的政策功底，

sentences.en: What that means is that climate change will now be an integral part of every major White House decision on national security and foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 将成为气候变化的代言人。

sentences.en: It will have a seat at the big boys and girls table, and John Kerry, who is a serious player and in many ways has more policy chops than a lot of the other people at that table,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一件大事。

sentences.en: will be the one speaking for climate change.
sentences.zh: 另一部分，约翰·克里的搭档，国内气候沙皇，将是吉娜·麦卡锡。

sentences.en: So I think that's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 她曾是奥巴马政府时期环境保护署的负责人，

sentences.en: The other sort of piece of that, John Kerry's partner, the domestic climate czar, will be Gina McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 她实际上是美国环保署削减所有主要经济部门二氧化碳排放法规的起草者。

sentences.en: She was the head of the Environmental Protection Agency in the Obama administration,
sentences.zh: 吉娜·麦卡锡现在将负责确保她的遗产得到恢复和加强。

sentences.en: and she actually was the author of the EPA regulations to cut CO2 emissions from all the biggest economic sectors.
sentences.zh: 这一次，她不仅是环保署的负责人。

sentences.en: Gina McCarthy will now be in charge of basically making sure that her legacy gets put back and strengthened.
sentences.zh: 她将在白宫任职，并将拥有权力来制定这些国内政策，并交给约翰·克里，这样他就可以在世界各地奔走并说，看，

sentences.en: This time, she won't just be head of the EPA.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们正在做的。

sentences.en: She'll be in the White House, and she will have the authority to deliver these domestic policies to hand over to John Kerry so he can go around the world and say, look,
sentences.zh: 我们是认真的。

sentences.en: this is what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 我们正在实现它。

sentences.en: We're serious.
sentences.zh: 你们也必须这样做。

sentences.en: We're getting it done.
sentences.zh: 好的，既然我们已经认识了这些气候沙皇，让我们谈谈他们将如何落实这一议程。

sentences.en: You've got to do it too.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Okay, so now that we've met these climate czars, let's talk about how they are going to be putting this agenda into place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拜登喜欢谈论那种应对气候变化的“全政府”方针，以及不同机构将要做的所有这些事情。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，其实就取决于三件事。

sentences.en: So, you know, Biden likes to talk about the sort of whole of government approach to climate change and all these things that different agencies are going to do.
sentences.zh: 美国经济中有三个主要的温室气体排放源。

sentences.en: Really, at the end of the day, though, it comes down to three things.
sentences.zh: 这块饼图的三个部分。

sentences.en: There are three main sources of planet warming greenhouse gases in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果你想解决这个问题，你必须大幅削减这三者中的每一项。

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 首先是汽车污染。

sentences.en: Three pieces of that pie.
sentences.zh: 这是美国温室气体的头号来源。

sentences.en: And if you want to solve the problem, you have to drastically cut each one of these.
sentences.zh: 占了三分之一多一点。

sentences.en: And that is pollution from cars.
sentences.zh: 第二，发电厂污染。

sentences.en: That is a number one contributor to greenhouse gases in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们如何开启灯光。

sentences.en: It's a little over a third.
sentences.zh: 第三，虽然听起来奇怪，但非常重要，那就是石油和天然气井的甲烷泄漏。

sentences.en: Number two, pollution from power plants.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点晦涩。

sentences.en: How we turn on the lights.
sentences.zh: 原因如下。

sentences.en: And number three, weird, but it's a big deal, is leaking methane emissions from oil and gas wells.
sentences.zh: 甲烷就像一种超级力量，是超级充电版的二氧化碳。

sentences.en: That sounds sort of obscure.
sentences.zh: 它的吸热能力是二氧化碳的50多倍。

sentences.en: And here's the reason why.
sentences.zh: 如果你能解决这个问题，你就实际上已经大幅削减了来自美国经济的温室气体，即那些吸热气体。

sentences.en: Methane is like a superpower, supercharged CO2.
sentences.zh: 这就是那三件事。

sentences.en: It has over 50 times the heat trapping power of carbon dioxide.
sentences.zh: 如果美国联邦政府能够制定出能够大幅削减这三种排放的政策，这就是解决方案。

sentences.en: And if you get at that, you've actually taken a really big bite of the greenhouse gases, the heat trapping gases that are coming from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们如何削减排放并实现这些目标的方法。

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他听起来很不错且会有所帮助的事情。

sentences.en: Those are the three things.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不解决这三点，你就无法实现目标。

sentences.en: If the U.S.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们逐一讨论这些问题。

sentences.en: federal government can put in place policies that can drastically cut those three emissions, that's the solution.
sentences.zh: 汽车、发电厂、甲烷泄漏，以及拜登的议程将如何解决所有这些问题。

sentences.en: That's how we cut our emissions and reach these goals.
sentences.zh: 让我们从汽车开始。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of other stuff that sounds really nice and that will help.
sentences.zh: 拜登在汽车方面的议程是什么？

sentences.en: But if you don't do those, you won't get there.
sentences.zh: 谈论拜登的议程在很多方面——我想拜登可能不太喜欢这样——但你必须首先谈谈奥巴马的议程。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's talk about these one at a time.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马实施了一项极其激进的法规，旨在大幅削减汽车的化石燃料排放。

sentences.en: Cars, power plants, methane leaks, and how the Biden agenda will address all of them.
sentences.zh: 他实施了燃油经济性标准，要求汽车制造商制造和销售到2025年平均油耗达到每加仑54英里的汽车。

sentences.en: And let's start with cars.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常激进的目标。

sentences.en: What is the Biden agenda on cars?
sentences.zh: 基本上，一旦他们实施了这一政策，就意味着每一家想要在美国销售汽车的汽车制造商都必须立即开始投资制造和销售电动汽车。

sentences.en: So to talk about the Biden agenda in so many ways, and I think Biden probably doesn't love this, but you have to first talk a little bit about the Obama agenda.
sentences.zh: 我们正在进行中。

sentences.en: So Obama put in place an incredibly aggressive regulation to drastically cut fossil fuel emissions from cars.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He put in place fuel economy standards that would have required automakers to build and sell cars that reach an average of 54 miles per gallon by 2025.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That is a very aggressive goal.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And basically, once they put that in place, it meant that every automaker who wants to sell in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: had to immediately start investing in building and selling electric vehicles.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That was the vision.
sentences.zh: 这就是最初的愿景。

sentences.en: And then the Trump administration came in, and as soon as Trump was elected, the CEO of GM went and met with Trump in the Oval Office and said, hey, can you roll these back for us?
sentences.zh: 后来特朗普政府上台了，特朗普一当选，通用汽车的首席执行官就去白宫椭圆形办公室见了特朗普，说，嘿，你能帮我们把这些规定撤销吗？

sentences.en: Which they did.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: So the Biden plan is essentially to put that back in place.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登的计划本质上就是把那些规定重新落实到位。

sentences.en: The numbers might not be exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 数字可能不会完全一样。

sentences.en: One difference is, you know, that regulation was put in place 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 其中一个区别是，你知道，那项法规是十年前制定的。

sentences.en: It applied to cars in 2025.
sentences.zh: 它适用于2025年的汽车。

sentences.en: They're going to have to go out a lot further than that.
sentences.zh: 他们将不得不把目标定得更远。

sentences.en: The timing is different.
sentences.zh: 时间安排不同了。

sentences.en: The economy is different.
sentences.zh: 经济形势也不同了。

sentences.en: One really big thing that is very different for the Biden administration as it prepares to reimpose these tough, tough fuel economy standards for cars is the auto industry.
sentences.zh: 对于拜登政府来说，在准备重新实施这些严苛的汽车燃油经济性标准时，有一个非常大的不同点，那就是汽车行业。

sentences.en: The auto industry fought tooth and nail against the Obama administration putting those rules in place.
sentences.zh: 汽车行业曾竭力反对奥巴马政府实施这些规则。

sentences.en: But what has happened now, and actually in the news of last week, is that same CEO of GM, Mary Barra,
sentences.zh: 但现在发生的情况，实际上也是上周的新闻，就是那位通用汽车的首席执行官玛丽·巴拉，

sentences.en: announced that GM is now getting ready to do a total U-turn and go to 100% electric vehicles and even stop producing combustion engines.
sentences.zh: 宣布通用汽车现在准备来个彻底的大转弯，转向100%的电动汽车，甚至停止生产内燃机汽车。

sentences.en: This is a huge, huge tailwind for the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 这对拜登政府来说是一个巨大、巨大的推动力。

sentences.en: And several other auto companies are also on board and are kind of expected to publicly come out in the next week or so saying, we will do this.
sentences.zh: 其他几家汽车公司也加入了进来，预计在未来一周左右会公开表态说，我们也会这样做。

sentences.en: And that's partly because the global auto market has transformed so much in the last decade.
sentences.zh: 这在一定程度上是因为全球汽车市场在过去十年里发生了巨大的转变。

sentences.en: This is where the market is going.
sentences.zh: 这就是市场的发展方向。

sentences.en: Other countries now have standards like this in place.
sentences.zh: 其他国家现在也实施了这样的标准。

sentences.en: The automakers have to sell to a global market.
sentences.zh: 汽车制造商必须面向全球市场销售。

sentences.en: So the difference is that this time when Biden goes to put those car rules back in place, he will actually have all the auto companies at the table with him working,
sentences.zh: 所以不同之处在于，这一次当拜登要重新实施这些汽车规则时，他实际上会让所有的汽车公司都坐在谈判桌前与他合作，

sentences.en: prepared to sign on to something from day one.
sentences.zh: 准备从第一天起就签署协议。

sentences.en: So interestingly, the auto industry is on board with this vision, the one you described at the start of our conversation, that includes electric cars.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，汽车行业支持这一愿景，也就是你在我们谈话开始时描述的那个愿景，其中就包括电动汽车。

sentences.en: And cars are the biggest source of emission and therefore the biggest obstacle to starting to lower the biggest source of emissions, which would be car companies saying no way,
sentences.zh: 汽车是最大的排放源，因此也是开始降低最大排放源的最大障碍，而这原本会是汽车公司说“没门”的地方，

sentences.en: that has started to melt away.
sentences.zh: 现在这种阻力已经开始消融了。

sentences.en: Yes, this is a really big deal.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实是一件大事。

sentences.en: I think that that will probably stand as the biggest thing that the Biden administration will end up doing on climate change.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能会成为拜登政府在气候变化方面最终所做的最重要的事情。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息，去探索《纽约时报》呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》的订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载时报应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Coral, let's talk about the second major source of emissions that you had mentioned, power plants.
sentences.zh: 那么，科拉尔，我们来谈谈你提到的第二个主要排放源：发电厂。

sentences.en: What is the Biden plan for those?
sentences.zh: 拜登对这些发电厂有什么计划？

sentences.en: They don't know.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道。

sentences.en: With power plants, it gets really murky.
sentences.zh: 对于发电厂，情况变得非常模糊。

sentences.en: And here is why.
sentences.zh: 原因如下。

sentences.en: Obama tried to do regulations on power plants.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马曾试图对发电厂进行监管。

sentences.en: He did a whole big regulation that required states to shut down coal plants, build wind and solar.
sentences.zh: 他制定了一项宏大的法规，要求各州关闭燃煤电厂，建设风能和太阳能设施。

sentences.en: That was going to be it.
sentences.zh: 本该就是这样。

sentences.en: Even before the legal fight got to the Supreme Court, the Supreme Court justice, Justice Roberts, put a stay on that plan,
sentences.zh: 甚至在法律斗争到达最高法院之前，最高法院大法官罗伯茨就对该计划发布了暂缓执行令，

sentences.en: which essentially meant this plan does not get implemented until all of these lawsuits about it get legally resolved.
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着在所有关于该计划的诉讼在法律上得到解决之前，该计划无法实施。

sentences.en: That is a very clear sign that the Supreme Court thinks it's a loser.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常明确的信号，表明最高法院认为该计划注定会失败。

sentences.en: And so it was never implemented.
sentences.zh: 所以它从未被实施。

sentences.en: And so now it's kind of stuck in the courts.
sentences.zh: 现在它在法院里陷入了僵局。

sentences.en: But as the Biden administration goes back and tries to do this again, they know that already the legal outlook is not good.
sentences.zh: 但当拜登政府回头试图再次这样做时，他们知道法律前景已经不容乐观。

sentences.en: And very, very importantly, this Supreme Court is even more conservative than the Supreme Court during the Obama administration.
sentences.zh: 而且非常、非常重要的一点是，现在的最高法院比奥巴马政府时期的最高法院更加保守。

sentences.en: So if you can't do it with regulation, well, can you do it through Congress?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果不能通过法规来做到这一点，那么，能通过国会来实现吗？

sentences.en: That is a very tough sell as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个非常难推销的方案。

sentences.en: As you know, Democrats have a 51-vote majority, including the tie-breaking vote of Vice President Harris.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，民主党拥有51票的多数席位，其中包括副总统哈里斯的决定性一票。

sentences.en: You need a 60-vote majority just to get anything onto the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 你需要60票的多数才能让任何法案进入参议院讨论。

sentences.en: And if you were to bring a bill to Congress that essentially said we're going to shut down coal plants and replace them with wind and solar,
sentences.zh: 如果你要向国会提交一项法案，本质上说我们要关闭燃煤电厂并用风能和太阳能取而代之，

sentences.en: it's very hard to see how you even get all of the Democrats to vote for that.
sentences.zh: 很难想象你甚至能让所有的民主党人都投票支持它。

sentences.en: And the particular Democrat who you'd be looking at is Senator Joe Manchin from West Virginia,
sentences.zh: 而你特别关注的那位民主党人是来自西弗吉尼亚州的参议员乔·曼钦，

sentences.en: a major coal state who is a huge opponent of the Obama Clean Power Plan and has supported the Trump rollbacks of regulation.
sentences.zh: 他所在的州是主要的产煤州，他是奥巴马《清洁电力计划》的坚定反对者，并支持特朗普撤销监管。

sentences.en: It's very hard to see how you get a simple Democratic majority for some kind of legislation in Congress that would shut down coal plants.
sentences.zh: 很难想象你如何能在国会获得简单的民主党多数票来通过某种关闭燃煤电厂的立法。

sentences.en: So that one, at this moment, you know, unless they can do some really amazing legal tap dancing in reproducing this regulation,
sentences.zh: 所以，目前这一项，你知道，除非他们能在重新制定这项法规时跳出令人惊叹的法律华尔兹，

sentences.en: or unless there's some kind of very interesting breakthrough in Congress,
sentences.zh: 或者除非国会能出现某种非常有趣的突破，

sentences.en: it is hard to see how this administration is able to meaningfully do a big policy that takes a bite out of power plant emissions.
sentences.zh: 否则很难看出这届政府如何能够有意义地制定一项大政策来削减发电厂的排放。

sentences.en: So the second largest source of emissions, coal plants, is kind of a fly in the ointment of the Biden vision here.
sentences.zh: 所以第二大排放源——燃煤电厂，在拜登的愿景中有点像汤里的一只苍蝇。

sentences.en: They don't really know exactly what to do about it.
sentences.zh: 他们真的不知道该怎么处理它。

sentences.en: They're trying to figure it out, but right now there is not a clear legal or legislative path for them to put a policy in place.
sentences.zh: 他们正在努力想办法，但目前还没有明确的法律或立法途径让他们实施政策。

sentences.en: And finally, methane.
sentences.zh: 最后是甲烷。

sentences.en: What is the plan for that?
sentences.zh: 对此有什么计划？

sentences.en: So, once again, just like cars and just like power plants, Obama put a rule in place saying companies have to inspect leaks, plug them up, keep them under control.
sentences.zh: 所以，再一次，就像汽车和发电厂一样，奥巴马制定了一条规则，要求公司检查泄漏、堵住漏洞并将其控制住。

sentences.en: Trump rolled it back.
sentences.zh: 特朗普撤销了它。

sentences.en: When Trump rolled back the rule, he actually said the federal government doesn't have to regulate methane at all.
sentences.zh: 当特朗普撤销该规则时，他实际上说联邦政府根本不需要监管甲烷。

sentences.en: Basically, in this case, I think it's almost cut and paste.
sentences.zh: 基本上，在这种情况下，我认为这几乎是直接照搬。

sentences.en: The Biden people can go back in, take that Obama rule, and put it back.
sentences.zh: 拜登团队可以回去，拿出那条奥巴马时期的规则，然后重新实施。

sentences.en: It'll probably take a year or two before it is implemented, but the expectation is there's a pretty clear path to do it, and it won't be too hard.
sentences.zh: 实施可能需要一两年时间，但预期是有一条相当明确的途径可以做到，而且不会太难。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court won't stand in the way of it.
sentences.zh: 最高法院也不会阻挠它。

sentences.en: This is one where the law is pretty clear about giving the executive branch the authority to do this.
sentences.zh: 这是法律相当明确地赋予行政部门权力的领域。

sentences.en: The chances appear favorable before the Supreme Court, even this very conservative Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 即使在非常保守的最高法院面前，胜算似乎也很大。

sentences.en: So that's one where they're moving ahead fairly confidently.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们相当自信地推进的一项。

sentences.en: Coral, if Biden gets done what he wants to get done on these three areas, what will be the economic cost of having done it, specifically on jobs?
sentences.zh: 科拉尔，如果拜登在这些领域实现了他想要的目标，那么这样做的经济成本是多少，特别是在就业方面？

sentences.en: I know that Biden is very sensitive to that question, and that, of course, is the leading objection from Republicans and moderate Democrats in some of these key states where,
sentences.zh: 我知道拜登对这个问题非常敏感，当然，这也是共和党人和一些关键州温和派民主党人的主要反对意见，在这些州，

sentences.en: for example, there are coal-fired power plants, and there is gas drilling, and there is oil exploration.
sentences.zh: 例如，有燃煤电厂，有天然气钻探，还有石油勘探。

sentences.en: So Biden is being very candid about this, that aggressive environmental and climate policies will cost jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登对此非常坦诚，承认激进的环境和气候政策会付出就业代价。

sentences.en: He has acknowledged that essentially what his plan will do will ultimately end the coal industry, shrink the oil industry down to a fraction of its former size,
sentences.zh: 他承认，他的计划本质上最终将终结煤炭工业，将石油工业缩小到其原有规模的一小部分，

sentences.en: and that that necessarily costs jobs and hurts communities.
sentences.zh: 而这必然会造成失业并伤害社区。

sentences.en: In being candid about that, he also says that he believes that the jobs created in wind and solar manufacturing, in installation,
sentences.zh: 在坦诚这一点时，他也表示他相信风能和太阳能制造及安装领域创造的就业机会，

sentences.en: that there will be an equal or greater number of jobs created by these regulations.
sentences.zh: 这些法规创造的就业岗位数量将相等或更多。

sentences.en: And I should say, he's backed by economists in that.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，他得到了经济学家的支持。

sentences.en: Economists do generally say that when you lose a certain number of jobs in fossil fuel or polluting industries,
sentences.zh: 经济学家普遍认为，当你失去化石燃料或污染行业的一定数量的就业岗位时，

sentences.en: you do tend to gain about an equal number of jobs in environmental mitigation and cleaner industries.
sentences.zh: 你往往会在环境治理和更清洁的行业中获得大致相同数量的就业岗位。

sentences.en: The problem is, how do you match those skills and people up?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你如何匹配这些技能和人员？

sentences.en: Can you necessarily take a coal miner who has lost his job in Appalachia or Wyoming and move him and his family to a solar plant manufacturing place in Nevada?
sentences.zh: 你是否一定能让一个在阿巴拉契亚或怀俄明州失业的煤矿工人，带着他的家人搬到内华达州的太阳能工厂工作？

sentences.en: You know, what Biden is doing is he's saying that the government is here to help.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拜登的做法是说政府会在这里提供帮助。

sentences.en: We're going to have funding to go into these communities to figure out how to retrain,
sentences.zh: 我们将有资金投入这些社区，找出如何进行再培训的方法，

sentences.en: to figure out how to bring the manufacturing of the new technologies to the places where the old jobs are going.
sentences.zh: 找出如何将新技术的制造带到旧工作岗位流失的地方。

sentences.en: He is making a good faith effort to try to match those up.
sentences.zh: 他正在真诚地努力尝试将两者匹配起来。

sentences.en: I think that's a very hard challenge.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常艰巨的挑战。

sentences.en: It's not necessarily clear that it's always going to work.
sentences.zh: 不一定清楚这是否总是有效。

sentences.en: But the fact is that climate change, it has already wreaked a significant economic cost on our economy as well.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，气候变化已经对我们的经济造成了巨大的经济损失。

sentences.en: Biden and his appointees are trying to make the point that, like, you pay one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 拜登和他的任命官员试图指出，就像，你迟早都要付出代价。

sentences.en: And we're already starting to pay.
sentences.zh: 而且我们已经开始付出代价了。

sentences.en: It feels like a lot of what we are talking about here in the Biden climate plan is restoring regulations from the Obama administration that were reversed by the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们在这里讨论的很多拜登气候计划，都是在恢复被特朗普政府推翻的奥巴马政府时期的法规。

sentences.en: And by definition, that means that once put in place, they can be reversed by the next president if that happens to be a Republican.
sentences.zh: 根据定义，这意味着一旦实施，如果下一任总统恰好是共和党人，它们就可以被推翻。

sentences.en: Because we talked about this a lot on the show in the last couple of days, the only real permanence in American government comes from laws passed by Congress.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在过去几天里在节目中讨论了很多这个问题，美国政府中唯一真正的持久性来自于国会通过的法律。

sentences.en: And like you said, this does not seem to be a Congress, especially a Senate, that is likely to pass sweeping environmental programs at the moment.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这似乎不是一个国会，尤其是参议院，目前不太可能通过全面的环境计划。

sentences.en: So where does that really leave the Biden administration?
sentences.zh: 那么这到底让拜登政府处于什么境地？

sentences.en: They know that so well, particularly in this space of climate regulations.
sentences.zh: 他们非常清楚这一点，特别是在气候法规这个领域。

sentences.en: They just watched Exhibit A, all the rules in place.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚目睹了例证A，所有的规则都到位了。

sentences.en: They all went away.
sentences.zh: 它们全都消失了。

sentences.en: They're all putting them back.
sentences.zh: 他们现在都在把它们放回去。

sentences.en: They have that at top of mind.
sentences.zh: 他们对此铭记在心。

sentences.en: And I think that what President Biden would like more than anything else would indeed be any kind of permanent law.
sentences.zh: 我认为拜登总统最想要的确实是任何形式的永久性法律。

sentences.en: And I think that what the rest of the world is really looking for from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为世界其他国家真正从美国寻求的，

sentences.en: is any kind of permanent law.
sentences.zh: 也是任何形式的永久性法律。

sentences.en: I mean, if John Kerry is going to be going around the world saying, oh, look, we're going to do all these regulations.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果约翰·克里要在世界各地说，哦，看，我们要制定所有这些法规。

sentences.en: They're going to be like, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，等一下。

sentences.en: Didn't you guys just do a bunch of regulations and they went away?
sentences.zh: 你们不是刚制定了一堆法规，然后它们就消失了吗？

sentences.en: Like, we need to see something from you that will stick.
sentences.zh: 我们需要看到你们拿出一些能持久的东西。

sentences.en: And they they know that.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这一点。

sentences.en: And they also know, as you said, that the goal is permanent legislation.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们也知道目标是永久性立法。

sentences.en: The goal is a law that will outlast Democrats and Republicans and not just administration, but the lives of the presidents and the legislators who enact them.
sentences.zh: 目标是一项能够超越民主党和共和党，不仅超越政府任期，而且超越制定它们的总统和立法者寿命的法律。

sentences.en: And right now it is not looking like that is in the cards for climate change.
sentences.zh: 而现在看来，气候变化似乎并不具备这种条件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which I'm sure is pretty depressing to John Kerry and to Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我相信这对约翰·克里和乔·拜登来说是相当令人沮丧的。

sentences.en: So is the reality that we are going to be left with a kind of sweeping and ultimately impermanent Biden climate change vision?
sentences.zh: 那么现实情况是我们最终将只剩下一个既全面又最终不稳定的拜登气候变化愿景吗？

sentences.en: And is that just where we are going to be?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们要面对的现实吗？

sentences.en: The answer to that is it depends.
sentences.zh: 答案是视情况而定。

sentences.en: I think if the next administration is Republican, certainly there will be a powerful drive to deregulate.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果下一届政府是共和党政府，肯定会有强大的去监管动力。

sentences.en: And certainly these regulations that affect the fossil fuel economy will come under scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些影响化石燃料经济的法规将受到审查。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: But even under those Republican administrations, I do think that there is likely to be a moment because there has been this significant shift from some major corporations.
sentences.zh: 但即使在那些共和党政府下，我也确实认为可能会有一个转折点，因为一些大公司已经发生了重大转变。

sentences.en: And here I'm thinking very much of these big auto companies of GM and Ford, these big, iconic, essential American manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我非常想到这些大型汽车公司，通用汽车和福特，这些大型、标志性、至关重要的美国制造商。

sentences.en: Once these regulations really are put in place and these companies have invested in the kinds of cards they're going to build 10 and 15 years out,
sentences.zh: 一旦这些法规真正落实到位，这些公司在未来10到15年内要制造的汽车类型上进行了投资，

sentences.en: as much as they don't like regulations, they hate even more the uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们不喜欢监管，但他们更讨厌不确定性。

sentences.en: They don't want that whiplash.
sentences.zh: 他们不想要那种剧烈的波动。

sentences.en: And I think in some cases, some of these rules, and I think the car rules are a good candidate for this.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某些情况下，其中一些规则，我认为汽车规则就是一个很好的候选者。

sentences.en: Once they get in place and the industry just gets fully on board and they get baked in, if the industry is not going to the White House and saying, hey, make these go away,
sentences.zh: 一旦它们落实到位，行业完全接受并将其内化，如果行业不再去白宫说，嘿，让这些消失吧，

sentences.en: that is something that could help keep them baked in.
sentences.zh: 那将有助于保持它们的稳定性。

sentences.en: In other words, the permanence of this vision may rest with industry as much as with government.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这一愿景的持久性可能既取决于行业，也取决于政府。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The reality is that climate change is here and it affects those industries, too.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是气候变化已经到来，它也影响着这些行业。

sentences.en: They see it.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了。

sentences.en: They get it.
sentences.zh: 他们明白了。

sentences.en: And that would be less about altruism than also just about kind of baking things in for the way in which climate change has changed economic reality for us in a completely new way.
sentences.zh: 这与其说是出于利他主义，不如说是因为气候变化以一种全新的方式改变了我们的经济现实，从而将这些因素内化。

sentences.en: Thank you, Coral.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，科拉尔。

sentences.en: We appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: Always a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 总是很高兴。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: During a meeting at the White House on Monday night, 10 moderate Republican senators, led by Susan Collins of Maine,
sentences.zh: 周一晚上在白宫的一次会议上，由缅因州的苏珊·柯林斯领导的10位温和派共和党参议员，

sentences.en: presented President Biden with a plan for a narrow $618 billion economic stimulus plan that they said would garner bipartisan support.
sentences.zh: 向拜登总统提交了一项6180亿美元的精简经济刺激计划，他们称该计划将获得两党的支持。

sentences.en: His view is that the size of the package needs to be commensurate with the dual crises we're facing, hence why he proposed a package that's $1.9 trillion.
sentences.zh: 他的观点是，方案的规模必须与我们面临的双重危机相称，这就是他提出1.9万亿美元方案的原因。

sentences.en: But even before the meeting, White House Press Secretary Jen Psaki warned the senators that the president was committed to a plan that would cost more than three times as much,
sentences.zh: 但甚至在会议召开之前，白宫新闻秘书珍·普萨基就警告参议员们，总统致力于推行一项成本是该金额三倍以上的计划，

sentences.en: and that Biden may choose to push it through without Republican support.
sentences.zh: 而且拜登可能会选择在没有共和党支持的情况下强行通过。

sentences.en: The risk is not that it is too big, this package.
sentences.zh: 风险不在于这个方案规模太大。

sentences.en: The risk is that it is too small, and that remains his view.
sentences.zh: 风险在于它规模太小，而这依然是他的观点。

sentences.en: And the fallout from the stock market frenzy over GameStop spread on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一，围绕游戏驿站（GameStop）的股市狂潮所带来的影响进一步蔓延。

sentences.en: Robinhood, the online trading platform used by many investors to purchase the stock,
sentences.zh: 许多投资者用来购买该股票的在线交易平台Robinhood表示，

sentences.en: said it had raised an additional $2.5 billion to meet its financial requirements to support record trading volumes.
sentences.zh: 它已经额外筹集了25亿美元，以满足其支持创纪录交易量的财务需求。

sentences.en: And new data showed that the volume of short bets against shares of GameStop, which had motivated many small investors to purchase the stock, had fallen by half,
sentences.zh: 新数据显示，针对游戏驿站股票的空头押注规模——这曾促使许多小投资者购买该股票——已经减半，

sentences.en: as losses from those early bets mounted.
sentences.zh: 因为那些早期押注带来的损失在不断增加。

sentences.en: But as of Monday afternoon, GameStop shares had fallen $100, or more than 30%, to $225.
sentences.zh: 但截至周一下午，游戏驿站的股价已经下跌了100美元，跌幅超过30%，至225美元。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Michael Simon-Johnson, Eric Krupke, and Luke Vanderpluk.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊、埃里克·克鲁普克和卢克·范德普鲁克制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George and M.J.
sentences.zh: 由马克·乔治和M.J.编辑，

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn, and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音效设计。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Balbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
